**Part 4: Summarizing Countries, Regions, and Time Periods**

**Estimated time:** 2-3 hours

This assignment introduces grouped summaries. You will use `group_by()` and
`summarise()` to compare countries, regions, and years. Always check what one
row represents before and after summarizing.

## Why knit?

A successful knit confirms that your summaries can be rebuilt from the raw
assignment data in order.

## Packages and data

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
options(repos = c(CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org"))

if (!requireNamespace("tidyverse", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("tidyverse")
}

library(tidyverse)

dev <- read_csv("../data/development_indicators_2026.csv")
dictionary <- read_csv("../data/development_indicators_dictionary_2026.csv")
```

## Summarizing one variable

Use `summarise()` to reduce a dataset to summary statistics.

```{r}
dev |>
  filter(assignment_sample == TRUE & year == 2023) |>
  summarise(
    mean_life_expectancy = mean(life_expectancy),
    median_life_expectancy = median(life_expectancy),
    n_countries = n()
  )
```

## Grouping by region

Use `group_by()` before `summarise()` to calculate statistics within groups.

```{r}
region_life_2023 <- dev |>
  filter(assignment_sample == TRUE & year == 2023) |>
  group_by(region) |>
  summarise(
    mean_life_expectancy = mean(life_expectancy),
    median_life_expectancy = median(life_expectancy),
    n_countries = n()
  )

region_life_2023
```

The unit of analysis changed. In `dev`, one row is a country-year. In
`region_life_2023`, one row is a region.

## Multiple grouping variables

You can group by more than one variable.

```{r}
region_year_life <- dev |>
  filter(assignment_sample == TRUE & year >= 2010) |>
  group_by(region, year) |>
  summarise(
    mean_life_expectancy = mean(life_expectancy),
    n_countries = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

head(region_year_life)
```

Plot the regional trend:

```{r}
region_year_life |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = mean_life_expectancy, color = region)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "Mean life expectancy",
    color = "Region",
    title = "Average Life Expectancy by Region",
    subtitle = "Assignment-sample countries, 2010-2024"
  )
```

## Missing values in summaries

Some indicators have missing values. By default, `mean()` returns `NA` if any
input value is missing.

```{r}
dev |>
  filter(assignment_sample == TRUE & year == 2023) |>
  summarise(mean_poverty = mean(poverty_rate))
```

Use `na.rm = TRUE` to remove missing values from the calculation.

```{r}
dev |>
  filter(assignment_sample == TRUE & year == 2023) |>
  summarise(
    mean_poverty = mean(poverty_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
    countries_with_poverty_data = sum(!is.na(poverty_rate)),
    total_countries = n()
  )
```

Missingness is substantive. Poverty data are usually based on household surveys,
which are not available every year in every country.

## Mean versus median

Means can be sensitive to outliers. Medians are often useful for skewed
variables like GDP per capita.

```{r}
dev |>
  filter(assignment_sample == TRUE & year == 2023) |>
  group_by(region) |>
  summarise(
    mean_gdp_pc = mean(gdp_per_capita_ppp, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_gdp_pc = median(gdp_per_capita_ppp, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_countries = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```
